# Input corpus for the shared canonicalization fixtures.
# Add a line here, run `go run ./cmd/genfixtures`, review the diff in
# testdata/normalize.json, then run both test suites.
# Blank lines and lines starting with '#' are ignored. Leading/trailing
# whitespace is part of the input, so quote-free lines are used as-is.

# basics
HTTP://Evil.COM:8080/a/./b/../c?x=1#frag
https://evil.com
https://evil.com/
evil.com/x
http://EVIL.com/UPPER
http://evil.com:443/x
http://evil.com:80/x
https://user:pw@evil.com./login.php?
http://user@evil.com/x
http://evil.com/#frag
http://evil.com/?
   http://evil.com/x

# path cleaning
https://evil.com//x//y/
http://evil.com/./././
http://evil.com/a/../../b
http://evil.com/%2e%2e/a
http://evil.com/..%2f..%2fetc/passwd
http://EVIL.COM./A//B/../C/./?Q=%41%2f%3f

# percent-encoding
https://evil.com/a%2520b
http://evil.com/a%2520%2525b
http://evil.com/a%3Fb
http://evil.com/a b
http://evil.com/%%%
http://evil.com/%7euser/
http://evil.com/x?y=%2520
http://evil.co.uk/path%20with%20space/?a=b%26c
http://evil.com/%E4%B8%AD%E6%96%87
https://xn--bcher-kva.example/%c3%bc/x

# query
http://evil.com/a?b=1?2
http://evil.com/a/b/c/d/e/f?x=1&y=2
http://tricky.com/a?b=c#d?e

# host forms
https://xn--bcher-kva.example/x
http://a..b.com/x
http://sub_domain.evil.com/x
http://ex-ample.com/x
http://xn--fsq.com/x
http://a.b.c/1/2.html?param=1/2
http://a.b.c.d.e/p1/p2/p3/p4/p5/p6
http://a.b.c.d.e.f.g.h.i.evil.com/x
https://a.b.evil.com/x/y/z/w/login.php?t=1

# rejected
https://1.2.3.4/x
https://[2001:db8::1]/x
http://0x7f000001/
http://127.1/x
ftp://evil.com/x
http://localhost/x
javascript:alert(1)

# misc
http://evil.com/x\y
http://evil.com/a\b\c
http://evil.com/a;b,c=d
http://evil.com/!$&'()*+,;=:@/x

# ftps / sftp are rewritten to https before parsing: non-special schemes get an
# opaque host from the WHATWG parser (no lowercasing, no IDNA, no %-decoding)
sftp://Evil.COM:22/a/./b/../c?x=1#frag
ftps://Evil.COM/a%2Fb
sftp://ev%69l.com/x
sftp://user@Bücher.example/x
sftp://evil.com/x\y
SFTP://evil.com/x
ftps://1.2.3.4/x

# percent-escaped hosts: WHATWG decodes once and rejects forbidden code points,
# net/url rejects every escape, so Go reproduces the WHATWG rule explicitly
https://ev%69l.com/x
https://ev%2Eil.com/
https://ev%C3%BCl.com/
https://ev%3Ail.com/
https://ev%40il.com/
https://ev%20il.com/
https://evil.com%2Fx/y
https://ev%2569l.com/
https://ev%25il.com/
https://ev%zzil.com/

# userinfo spoofing: the host is whatever follows the LAST '@', and '%' is legal
# in userinfo, so the forbidden-host-byte rule must not be applied to it
https://peichunyun.com%plcb%imbl@peichunyun.com/hlbn
https://evil.com%2Fx@real.com/y
https://u:p%25w@evil.com/x
https://a%40b@evil.com/x
https://real.com@evil.com/x
https://real.com@1.2.3.4/x

# homograph userinfo: U+2215 DIVISION SLASH fakes a path; the real host is the
# workers.dev name after the last '@'. net/url rejects non-ASCII userinfo.
https://fwbwqhlqgacv.com∕fwbwqhlqgacv∕x@generation-cover-8170.whdzq2qfs.workers.dev/
https://real∕bank.com@evil.com/login

# raw C0 / DEL bytes: WHATWG percent-encodes them, net/url rejects the URL
https://evil.com/ab
https://evil.com/ab
https://evil.com/a%00b
https://evil.com/x?q=ab

# labels may start or end with '-' (WHATWG CheckHyphens is off)
https://reduce-repair-.start.page/
https://-lead.example.com/x
https://a--b.com/x
https://x_y.example.com/
